title: Sell Mineral Rights in Chidester, AR
metaTitle: Sell Mineral Rights in Chidester, AR | Ouachita County
metaDescription: Small legacy oil interest near Chidester, Arkansas? We buy stripper-rate Smackover mineral rights in southern Ouachita County, priced off real current production.
heroLead: Chidester is a small crossroads community near the Calhoun County line, sitting over some of the oldest, slowest-producing wells left in the Ouachita County Smackover trend.
intro: This isn't an area where you'll find much new drilling activity. What you'll find instead are stripper wells drilled decades ago that are still limping along at low volumes, and mineral interests attached to them that have often gone unmanaged for years because the checks are small. Small doesn't mean the interest should be ignored, especially if it's one of several similar tracts a family has accumulated over generations.

sections.heading: Stripper wells near the county line
paragraphs: A stripper well by definition produces very little, often under ten barrels a day, but a group of them across a family's holdings can add up to a meaningful sale even if any single well's royalty check looks negligible. We look at the whole picture rather than dismissing a tract because one well's monthly statement is small.

sections.heading: Why old lease terms don't set today's price
paragraphs: Some Chidester-area leases date back decades, with royalty terms that were standard for their era but don't reflect current market structure. We don't price off the original lease terms; we price off current production, decline trend, and how similar interests in southern Ouachita County have traded recently.
If a well tied to your interest hasn't produced in years, we'll tell you that plainly rather than presenting a number based on outdated assumptions.

sections.heading: Verifying ownership on older, quieter interests
paragraphs: Interests around Chidester are frequently held by heirs who inherited a fraction without much documentation. We use the Ouachita County Circuit Clerk's records in Camden to trace and confirm ownership as part of the offer process, which is often the fastest path when the family paperwork itself is incomplete.

faqs.question: Our royalty check from the Chidester-area well is only a few dollars. Is it worth selling?
faqs.answer: Small individual checks are common on stripper wells. We evaluate the total position, including any other interests you hold, before giving a real number.

faqs.question: The well tied to our interest seems to have stopped producing. What now?
faqs.answer: We check current operator filings to confirm status. A shut-in or plugged well changes the offer but doesn't automatically zero it out.

faqs.question: We don't have a copy of the original lease. Can you still help?
faqs.answer: Yes. We can trace the lease and ownership chain through Ouachita County Circuit Clerk records using your legal description or an old royalty statement.
